Comparison

Omarchy vs CachyOS

Both are built on Arch. One hands you a finished keyboard driven desktop, the other tunes Arch for speed and lets you pick the desktop.

Independent editorial guide

Short answer

Pick Omarchy if you want a finished, keyboard driven Hyprland desktop that's set up for you, with themes, apps and hotkeys ready on day one. Pick CachyOS if you want Arch with performance tuned packages and kernels, and you'd like to choose your own desktop, from KDE Plasma and GNOME to COSMIC or Hyprland. Both use pacman and the AUR, so most Arch software works on either.

Should I pick Omarchy or CachyOS?

Omarchy suits you if

  • You like working from the keyboard and want a tiling desktop without building it yourself.
  • You want one opinionated setup with themes, hotkeys and a menu (Super + Space) for installing, updating and tweaking.
  • You're fine with a Limine boot menu and full disk encryption by default. Omarchy can take a whole drive or install into free space next to Windows.[omarchy.org]

CachyOS suits you if

  • You want packages compiled for newer CPUs. The CachyOS wiki says x86-64-v3 builds give a 5% to 20% uplift over generic x86-64, depending on workload.[wiki.cachyos.org]
  • You want to pick your desktop at install time, with 17 or more desktops and window managers on offer.[cachyos.org]
  • You want kernel choices, like linux-cachyos with the BORE scheduler, sched-ext, BMQ and RT options.[cachyos.org]

Side by side

OmarchyCachyOS
BaseBuilt on Arch Linux, the Hyprland tiling window manager and the Quickshell desktop kit. [omarchy.org]Built on Arch Linux with the same rolling-release model. [cachyos.org]
PackagesSoftware comes from Arch's core, extra and multilib repos plus the Omarchy Package Repository; the AUR is optional. Install with omarchy pkg add <package>. [omarchy.org]Every package compiled for x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 and Zen4 with LTO; core packages also get PGO and BOLT. [cachyos.org]
KernelNot a point the Omarchy manual compares.linux-cachyos kernel with a tuned scheduler, plus BORE, sched-ext, BMQ and RT options. [cachyos.org]
InstallerInstalls from an ISO, either full-disk or into free space next to another OS. Encryption is on by default. [omarchy.org]A graphical Calamares-based installer or a CLI installer. [cachyos.org]
DesktopKeyboard-driven Hyprland tiling desktop. Neovim is the default editor and Foot the default terminal. [omarchy.org]17+ desktops and window managers to pick at install, including KDE Plasma, GNOME, COSMIC and Hyprland. [cachyos.org]

More about Omarchy

  • Rolling release. New installs start on the stable channel, which follows an Omarchy Arch mirror kept one month behind the latest packages. [omarchy.org]
  • Secure Boot and/or TPM must be turned off in the BIOS to install. [omarchy.org]
  • Firewall on by default: all incoming traffic is blocked except LocalSend's port 53317, and SSH stays off until you enable it. [omarchy.org]

How do you install and update apps on each?

OmarchyCachyOS
Install apps (GUI)Omarchy menu: Install, then Package or AUR [omarchy.org]Shelly or Octopi [wiki.cachyos.org]
Install apps (terminal)omarchy pkg add <name>sudo pacman -S <name>
UpdateUpdate, then Omarchy, or omarchy update [omarchy.org]sudo pacman -Syu, Shelly or Octopi [wiki.cachyos.org]

On Omarchy, every package in the official Omarchy repository has a profile on this site with its exact omarchy pkg add command. See how to install apps on Omarchy, including installing several at once, or start with the best Omarchy apps to install first. Since both are Arch based, most apps you'd install on one exist for the other. The commands just differ.

How can I try each one?

Omarchy: download the ISO from omarchy.org, write it to a USB stick (the manual suggests balenaEtcher on Mac or Windows, caligula on Linux), turn off Secure Boot and TPM, and boot from the stick. To keep Windows, shrink a partition first and pick the free space install when the installer asks.[omarchy.org]

CachyOS: download the ISO from cachyos.org, write it to a USB stick and boot from it. The installer pulls packages online, so keep a wired or solid wifi connection.[wiki.cachyos.org]

Not sure your CPU gets CachyOS's optimized builds? The CachyOS wiki gives this check:

/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 --help | grep supported

If you see x86-64-v4 (supported, searched), your CPU can use the v4 repos.[wiki.cachyos.org]

Frequently asked questions

Is Omarchy better than CachyOS?

They aim at different things. Omarchy gives you a finished keyboard driven Hyprland desktop. CachyOS gives you performance tuned Arch packages and lets you choose the desktop. The better one is the one that fits how you work.

Is CachyOS faster than Omarchy?

CachyOS focuses on speed: it recompiles Arch packages for newer CPUs and ships tuned kernels, and its wiki cites a 5% to 20% uplift for x86-64-v3 builds over generic x86-64. Omarchy focuses on the desktop experience instead. We haven't run our own benchmarks, so we don't publish a number for either.

Can I use Hyprland on CachyOS?

Yes. Hyprland is one of the desktops you can pick in the CachyOS installer. Omarchy's own configs and menus are built for Omarchy, though.

Are both based on Arch Linux?

Yes. Both are rolling releases on Arch, both use pacman, and both can use the AUR.

Which is better for gaming?

Both can run Steam, Lutris and Heroic, since they're all Arch packages. CachyOS adds gaming focused kernel and package tuning. See Steam on Omarchy and gaming on Omarchy after Windows on this site. Steam on Omarchy, Gaming on Omarchy after Windows.

Can I dual boot Omarchy with Windows?

Yes. The Omarchy manual's Dual Boot Install chapter covers installing into free space next to Windows: shrink a Windows partition, choose the free space install, then run limine-scan to add Windows to the boot menu. It doesn't work with BitLocker on, since BitLocker encrypts the whole drive. Dual boot Windows and Omarchy.

How do I install apps on Omarchy?

Open the Omarchy menu with Super + Space, choose Install, then Package. Or run omarchy pkg add followed by the package name.
